cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: The Sorrel agent and I have both claimed first passage at the same bell. She has proposed, in writing, that we settle it by duel. I have accepted, in writing. I now find I do not know how a duel is conducted.

left.label: Second him
left.outcome: "You would? Duly. I shall need to know what a second does."

right.label: Forbid it on Company water
right.outcome: "Forbidden. I note I am relieved. I note I am also, irregularly, disappointed."

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: He accepted. In writing. With a citation. I was joking. I can't back down from a man who's cited the Compact at me. Pistols at dawn on the towpath. You're seconding him. Who do I get?

left.label: Solas
left.outcome: Solas agrees, weary. "I've seconded worse for less."

right.label: Wren
right.outcome: Wren agrees, delighted. "I've always wanted to hold a pistol legally."

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: The night before. I have read three accounts of duels and they disagree on every particular. I have written my will. I have left my statute book to you. I would like it noted that I am not afraid.

left.label: Suggest both fire wide
left.outcome: "Fire wide. Is that permitted?" It is, you say. "Duly. Then I shall."

right.label: Suggest he withdraw
right.outcome: "Withdraw. From a Sorrel agent. In writing." He cannot. You knew he could not.

cards.speaker: solas
cards.text: Dawn. Towpath. Half the town watching from the bank with breakfast. Two pistols I've loaded with powder and no ball, which nobody's asked me about. Crane's counting paces aloud. Vane's laughing. Somebody has to say 'fire'. It's the seconds' job. That's us.

left.label: Say it
left.outcome: Two bangs, no balls, a cloud of smoke. Crane is astonished to be alive. Vane bows. The town applauds.

right.label: Say 'stop' instead
right.outcome: You stop it. Both are relieved. Both pretend outrage. The town is disappointed and goes to breakfast.

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: Neither of us is dead and neither has first passage and the whole town saw us make fools of ourselves. He shook my hand afterward. Matthias Crane shook my hand. What do I do with that?

left.label: Dine with him
left.outcome: They dine. They argue for two hours about fish. It is the start of something neither will name.

right.label: Nothing; it was a duel
right.outcome: "Nothing. Right." She does not do nothing. She sends him a fish.

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: I have drafted a schedule for precedence disputes that does not involve pistols. The Sorrel agent has signed it. I have signed it. It requires the Keeper's signature. I note this is the first Compact amendment in twenty-two years.

left.label: Sign it
left.outcome: The Halfway Precedence Schedule. Both shores ratify it within the year, baffled. Crane is happier than you have seen him.

right.label: The Keeper decides, as ever
right.outcome: "As ever. Duly. I shall keep the draft. It will keep."

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: Four cases of the shakes this week, all from the low street, all regulars at the Wheel. Same symptoms as bad water. Ilse says her ale is spring water. I would like to test the well. She will not let me.

left.label: Tell Ilse to let her
left.outcome: Ilse lets her, glaring. Stroud takes a bottle. Ilse takes it personally.

right.label: Test the pound instead
right.outcome: Stroud tests the pound. Iron, and something else. She looks toward the inn.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Your physician's been at my well with a bottle. Twenty years that well's fed this town and now it's poison because four drunks have the shakes. It's spring water. It comes up cold from the hill. Everyone knows that. Tell her.

left.label: It comes up from the pound
left.outcome: "Does it." She knows. She has always known. She is furious that you said it.

right.label: I'll tell her to stop
right.outcome: "Do." You do. Stroud does not stop. She tests it at night.

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: The well is the pound. Pound water, through a crack in the rock, with iron and, this month, something from the north bank I do not like. Boiled, it is fine. Ilse boils nothing. Ilse brews.

left.label: Order the ale boiled
left.outcome: Ilse boils it, swearing. The ale tastes of nothing. The shakes stop. Custom halves.

right.label: Let the town decide
right.outcome: You post Stroud's findings at the inn. Half stop drinking. Half drink more, to prove a point.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Fine. It's the pound. My father showed me the crack when I was twelve and told me never to say. The Company would charge for the water or close the well. Twenty years. Are you going to close me?

left.label: No; the town needs its inn
left.outcome: "Then we understand each other." She pours one from the well and drinks it herself.

right.label: Tell the Company; pay for the water
right.outcome: Vosk assesses a water rate. It is small. Ilse pays it. She does not forgive it.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: The brewery well. I've measured it against the gauge for a month. It rises and falls with the pound, a day behind. The pound's leaking into the rock under the town. Sorry. It's been doing it eighty years.

left.label: Where does the leaked water go?
left.outcome: "South. Under the town. Into the ground. Some of the fall each watch is that. Not much. Some."

right.label: Can the crack be sealed?
right.outcome: "Roughly. It'd close Ilse's well. She'd rather the leak."

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The shakes are gone. I boil what I have to. The town drinks Iron Spring and knows what it is now and drinks it anyway, because it's ours. Stroud and I are speaking again. First round's on the house.

left.label: Drink it
left.outcome: Iron Spring. It tastes of the pound. It tastes of Halfway.

right.label: Toast Stroud
right.outcome: Ilse toasts her too, eventually. The inn cheers, mostly at the free round.

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: My coal crews want the chapel blessing before passage. All forty boats. They've heard the grain boats get it. It's superstition and it costs me a morning a fleet. Stop it, or make it for everyone. Pick.

left.label: Blessings for everyone
left.outcome: Hale blesses coal. It takes all morning. The crews are delighted. Vane is not.

right.label: Blessings are the chapel's business
right.outcome: "Fine. Then my crews will queue at the chapel instead of the gate, and that's your morning gone too."

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: The coal crews have asked for the blessing. The rite speaks of still water and grain. I have adapted it: still water and warmth. The Concordance in Aldmere will not approve. I did not ask.

left.label: Bless the coal
left.outcome: "For the warmth that comes of fire and the fire that comes of the hill." The crews weep. Nobody expected that.

right.label: Stick to the rite as written
right.outcome: She blesses coal with the grain rite. Nobody notices but her.

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: My crews say the blessed boats go faster. They don't; I've timed them. But they think so, and row harder, so they do. Now I'm paying for blessings. Give me a receipt. My principals will ask.

left.label: A receipt from the Coffers
left.outcome: You write Sorrel Freight a receipt for 'spiritual services'. Crane, later, is delighted by the category.

right.label: The chapel gives receipts
right.outcome: Hale gives a receipt. It is a blessing on paper. Vane's principals frame it, confused.

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: A letter from the Concordance in Aldmere. They call the coal blessing 'irregular' and wish it stopped. The coal crews wish it continued. I have never disobeyed the Concordance. I have never been asked by anyone who meant it so much.

left.label: Bless the coal; answer Aldmere later
left.outcome: She continues. Aldmere writes again. She loses the letter. It is the most disobedient thing she has done.

right.label: Stop; the Concordance is the Concordance
right.outcome: She stops. The coal crews stand at the chapel door anyway, caps off, and she blesses them without coal.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A coal barge has come up with a Concordance lamp burning in a glass box on its bow: blessed at Halfway, carried to Sorrel and back. The crew asks for it reblessed. Nine boats behind it have lamps.

left.label: Rebless the lamps
left.outcome: Nine lamps, one morning. The pound at dusk is lit like a festival by coal boats with chapel lamps.

right.label: A blessing lasts; move along
right.outcome: The lamps pass unreblessed. The crews are downcast. Hale, later, goes down to the wharf and does it anyway.

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: The Concordance has decided the coal blessing is 'a local devotion' and may continue. They sent a hymn about coal. It is very bad. The crews love it. I have never seen so many in the chapel who could not read the hymnal.

left.label: Sing the bad hymn
left.outcome: Forty coal men roaring a bad hymn. Hale conducts. It is, somehow, the holiest thing at the summit.

right.label: Sing Petronel's instead
right.outcome: Hale asks Petronel. Petronel sings. The coal men are silent. The hymn is not about coal. It is about a river.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things, and these are the hands' three things. Wages a day late, every month. No gloves in winter. And the Company store won't take Company scrip at face. They've asked me to ask you. I've asked.

left.label: Hear all three properly
left.outcome: You sit with the hands an hour. You cannot fix all three. You say so. They did not expect that.

right.label: Wages are the Company's timing
right.outcome: "Right. I'll tell them the Company. They know the Company."

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. The hands have heard you heard them. They've heard nothing's changed. And they've asked whether a Keeper who listens and does nothing is better than one who doesn't listen. I said I'd ask. I'm asking.

left.label: Fix the gloves, at least
left.outcome: Twelve pairs from the Coffers. One thing of three. It counts.

right.label: Listening is what I can do
right.outcome: "Right. I'll tell them that. They'll like it about as much as I do."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: The hands have sent me a letter. With three demands and eleven signatures. The Company does not receive letters from hands. It receives them from Keepers. Tell them that, kindly, and make it work.

left.label: Sign the letter yourself; send it up
left.outcome: Twelve signatures. Pell is aghast. Ardent is puzzled. Gloves arrive from Ardent, which has never happened.

right.label: Tell them kindly
right.outcome: You tell them. Kindly. They fold the letter and put it away. It comes out again, later, unkindly.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. The hands have stopped. Not struck; stopped. They're at the paddles and not turning them. They'll turn when the scrip's worth face at the store. The store's the Company's. The Company's in Ardent.

left.label: Make up the scrip difference from the Coffers
left.outcome: You pay the hands the difference in coin. The paddles turn. The chest is lighter. Vosk reads the entry twice.

right.label: Turn the paddles yourself
right.outcome: You and Mirren turn the paddles for a day. Eleven hands watch. By dusk, three help. By morning, all.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The hands drink here. I hear the three things every night. Here's a fourth, free: they'd follow you off a cliff if you asked plainly, and walk you to the stone if you lied once. Dace won't say that. I just did.

left.label: Then I'll ask plainly
left.outcome: You go to the lock house and tell the hands exactly what you can and cannot do. They listen. It is enough.

right.label: Dace should say it
right.outcome: "He won't. He's a corporal. Corporals report; they don't say."

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. The hands have their gloves. The store takes scrip at face, since Pell had a word he pretends he didn't. And wages are still a day late, which the hands say they'll live with. Two of three.

left.label: Two of three
left.outcome: "Two of three. Right." He almost smiles. The hands call it 'the Keeper's two' for years.

right.label: Three of three; I'll pay the day myself
right.outcome: You advance wages from your own pocket, monthly. The hands know. Dace says nothing about it, loudly.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: The chest is light. Everyone's is, this season. Mine is not. I lend to the town at one in ten and would lend to the post at one in twelve, kindly, because I like a Keeper who stays. Twenty marks?

left.label: Twenty marks
left.outcome: Twenty in. The bell on her door rings for you now. One in twelve, monthly, kindly.

right.label: Ten, and no more
right.outcome: "Ten. Prudent. I like prudent. Prudent pays."

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: The first payment. Kindly, on time. I mention that the interest is on the whole, not the balance, that this is written on the note, and that most people do not read the note. You did not read the note.

left.label: Pay it; read the note now
left.outcome: You read it. One in twelve, on the whole, monthly, until cleared. It is a long note.

right.label: Dispute the terms
right.outcome: "Dispute. Kindly. The note is the note. Vosk has a copy." Vosk does.

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: The Ledger has a page on Cole. Dray's hand: 'she owns the chapel, the inn's debt, half the low street and the Board's nephew's gambling paper. Do not owe her. If you must, owe her briefly.'

left.label: Clear the debt now, whatever it costs
left.outcome: You empty the chest into Cole's hands. The bell stops ringing for you. It is very quiet.

right.label: Owe her a while longer
right.outcome: The bell rings monthly. The interest is on the whole. Dray's hand was right.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: You are behind. I do not send men. I have sent the Company a copy of the note. I also have an alternative: the Keeper's discretion over mooring fees at the pound, assigned to me for the term. I collect; you are clear.

left.label: Assign the mooring fees
left.outcome: Cole collects the pound's mooring fees. The Hullfolk pay a landlady now. Bram hears of it.

right.label: Let the Company see the note
right.outcome: Vosk reads it. "Irregular. Both of you." She pays it from the maintenance fund and says nothing else, which is worse.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: You owed Cole. Everyone in this town has. She's never been unkind and she's never let anyone go. My inn was hers for six years. Whatever you gave her to get clear, I hope it wasn't the town's.

left.label: It wasn't the town's
left.outcome: "Good." She looks at you a moment. "Good."

right.label: It was the mooring fees
right.outcome: "The Reach's fees. To Cole." She does not say anything else. She does not need to.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: You are clear. Few are. I have torn the note in front of you, as I do. I have kept a copy, as I do. Should the post need me again, my door has a bell. I hope you never hear it. I have never hoped that before.

left.label: Thank her
left.outcome: "Do not. Kindly." She means it, which is new.

right.label: Ask why she hopes it
right.outcome: "Because you paid. Nobody pays. They give me things instead. I have enough things."
